findings: Multiple-copy experiment replaces single nearest neighbor with g2NN; many dense features improve but still miss copies. This supports explicit multiplicity/completeness qualification, not merely finding one match or imposing fixed small top-k.

Random64x64regions copied five times expose low-keypoint failures. The authors speculate high-entropy regions would improve SIFT/SURF but did not evaluate that alternative here; do not treat speculation as measured coverage.
Downsampling reduces detection with fixed thresholds; it changes signal and copied-region size. Reduced image success/performance cannot certify original-resolution recall.

TableV memory is feature-size-derived theoretical lower bound. Authors report actual implementation more than twice that amount and DCT/DWT peaks above20GB. Do not equate payload allocation estimates with measured peak RSS or total memory budget.
Feature,matching,postprocessing timings are distinct historical unoptimized measurements; no hardware-equivalent local comparison or speedup asserted.

Supplement chooses per-feature thresholds with clean+JPEGvariants using every base scene. Thresholds that improve clean-only F1 can degrade combined-transform F1. Robustness across distortions still does not establish content-disjoint heldout evaluation.
Main-paper recommendations combine cheap sparse and expensive dense examination, but permit remaining false positives/misses. Our all-case goal cannot be marked achieved from these recommendations.
